ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the left side a is a bar chart of monthly reservoir inflow. The inflow is very small from January to March, gradually increases from April to June, reaches the highest of the year in July, remains very high in August, is also relatively large in September, and decreases noticeably again from October to December. The right side b is a bar chart of monthly average water level. The water level is relatively low around spring, rises noticeably after entering summer as the inflow increases, remains at a relatively high water level in summer and autumn, and then drops slightly. Then reason: the peak of reservoir inflow is concentrated in July—August, indicating that runoff is mainly supplied by summer monsoon precipitation and belongs to China’s eastern monsoon region; there is no spring snowmelt-type flood peak in the figure, so regions with obvious snowmelt supply in Northeast China and the high mountains of Northwest China can be excluded; floods are concentrated in midsummer, which conforms to the characteristics of the Huai River Basin and the southern margin of North China, where precipitation is concentrated in July—August. Northern Anhui Province is located near the Huai River Basin, matching the annual variation characteristics of this reservoir’s inflow and water level.
